question: Should CodexBar adopt either Quotio quota-display change, and should the upstream monitor persist an explicit reviewed or skipped disposition for those commits?
rationale: The queue identifies possible external improvements, but deciding whether their UX and architecture fit CodexBar requires repository-owner judgment rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Review and record dispositions
options.body: Compare the two substantive Quotio fixes with CodexBar, then record each SHA as adopted or intentionally skipped so future queue runs are actionable.

options.title: Adopt a verified gap
options.body: Land a narrow CodexBar-native fix only if the comparison shows an observable missing or incorrect behavior.

options.title: Retire the recurring queue
options.body: Disable or redesign the upstream-monitor issue workflow if periodic external-change notices are not a useful maintenance signal.

recommendation.title: Review and record dispositions
recommendation.body: Compare the two substantive Quotio fixes with CodexBar, then record each SHA as adopted or intentionally skipped so future queue runs are actionable.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level upstream adoption and automation-retention decisions need the project owner’s product and maintenance judgment.
